newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds tread water before U.S. rate word.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds tread water before U.S. rate word.

text.p: Argentine bonds were flat to higher late morning Tuesday as the market trod water ahead of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
But traders said they expected no rate hike by the Federal Reserve, allowing the market to rise after the recent shake-out in the wake of falling U.S. Treasuries and stocks.
"The adjustment has passed. I do not think there are many people who would want to take profits at these levels," said a trader at a foreign bank.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond was flat at 95-3/8 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.12 to 119.15.
Another trader said that with the expected announcement of stable U.S. rates, "the market will be in a position to rise again."
